rows: Equipment: Elastimold joint for single-core cables 11, 20 kV 15, 25, 35 PCJ El SEWEDY ELASTIMOLD

sections_target.text: Introduction

rows: This document sets out the steps for installing an Elastimold joint for single-core 11, 20 kV cables, in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and the June 2000 installation instructions

The Elastimold joint is designed to be a permanent, fully insulated and directly buriable joint. The joint withstands the voltage marked on the outside of the joint body and can carry a current rating equal to that of the cable. The joint is used with extruded insulated cables (XLPE) or (EPR), using copper or aluminium ferrules according to the cable type

sections_target.text: Safety precautions
Do not touch, hold or move by hand any cable carrying electric power.
The cable must be isolated from all sources of electric power before installing the joint.
Any excessive tampering with the joint components may cause it to fail.

The joint parts must be installed by persons well trained in installation and in the safe use of high-voltage equipment; these instructions are not a substitute for the training and experience required in the field of safety, and they do not cover every possible emergency.
Failure to follow these instructions may cause damage to the joint and serious or fatal injuries.
Environmental precautions
Masks must be worn to protect the lungs from dust and from the chemical materials and solutions that may be used for cleaning.
Do not burn the waste resulting from joint installation work; it must be collected and sent to the waste collection point for recycling.
Tools, instruments and equipment used
Insulator, ferrule, PVC tape
Outer sheath, earthing copper
Armouring and clamps (for armoured cables)
Silicone grease, mastic tape
Cleaning fluid, sandpaper
Tin soldering or spring clip
Work steps to be carried out
First: Preparing the cable
1. Align the two cable ends to be jointed in a straight line.
2. Provide a common overlap of 150 mm between the two ends, as shown in the drawing.
3. Slide the outer protective tube over cable No. (1).
Second: Removing the sheath and armouring
1. Remove the outer sheath of one end over a length of 510 mm from the centre of the joint, and of the other end over a length of 230 mm from the centre of the joint.
2. For armoured cables:
A - Remove the armouring to the same dimensions as the outer sheath for each of the two ends.

B - Carefully remove the inner sheath, leaving a distance of 10 mm after the armouring, taking care not to scratch the copper tape beneath the inner sheath. C - Insert a clamp in each of the two ends (1, 2) to connect the armouring afterwards.

3. Remove the filler from both ends. Note: The position in which the excess is cut is the same position in which the ferrule is installed, to ensure the dimensions do not go outside those permitted in the table (before and after crimping).
Third: Preparing the phase
1. Slide the copper braid onto the phase on the side of cable No. (1).

2. Carefully remove the copper tape over a length of (ص+30 mm) from the end of cable (2) and over a length of (ى) from the end of cable (1), taking care not to scratch the outer semiconducting layer of the cable.

3. Carefully remove the outer semiconducting layer (using a suitable tool) from both cable ends over a length of (ص) (as shown in the table), to obtain a smooth, even surface, so that the end of the outer semiconducting layer is uniformly rounded and tapered.
4. Remove the XLPE insulation over the distance س as shown in the table, forming a conical (bevel) shape in the insulation at its start over a distance of 10 mm.
Warning: Do not cut, or do anything that would damage the insulation layer, the semiconducting layer or any part of the conductor, as this may damage or shorten the expected life of the conductor.
Fourth: Applying the tape
1. Clean the XLPE insulation of the phase of cable No. 1 with the cleaning fluid and cleaning cloths, in the direction of the arrow, and make sure it is sound and free of any defects or scratches.
2. Wrap a layer of tape around the conductor end of cable No. (1) to protect the housing during entry.

3. Cover the outer semiconducting layer of the phase of cable No. (1) with tape, starting the wrapping from the start of the copper tape inwards until reaching the XLPE insulation, as shown in the drawing.
Fifth: Inserting the joint
1. Make sure the conductor, the XLPE insulation and the tape on the phase of cable No. (1) are clean before the insulation enters.
2. Apply silicone grease to the insulation and the tape of the phase of cable No. (1), as shown in the drawing.
3. Push the housing in, pressing with a slight twist in the direction of the tape wrapping, until the XLPE insulation of the cable appears for approximately 20 mm.
Sixth: Installing the ferrules
1. Remove the PVC tape from the conductor end of cable No. (1).
2. Insert the ferrule into each of the two phases.
3. Check the dimensions (before crimping) so that the distance between the two insulation ends does not exceed the distance (ب) as in the table.

4. Crimp the ferrule. Check the dimensions (after crimping) so that the distance between the two insulation ends does not exceed the distance (أ) as in the table; if the distance is exceeded, the preparation must be repeated and another ferrule crimped.
5. Remove any burrs and sharp protrusions from the ferrule and make its surface smooth and clean.
Seventh: Installing the joint
1. Clean the XLPE insulation with the cleaning fluid and cleaning cloths (always clean in the direction of the arrows).
2. Grease the surface of the insulation and the conductor with the supplied silicone grease.

3. Pull the housing into the opposite phase (cable No. 2) by pulling with a slight twist until the start of the tape of the phase of cable No. (1) appears; remove it to expose the outer semiconducting layer on cable No. (1) over a length of 30 mm, and leave the rest of the tape. Grease the surface of the insulation and the conductor with the supplied silicone grease.

4. Pull the housing to its final position so that the part of the housing overlapping the outer semiconducting layer of the phase at both ends is equal; this is noticed by touch or by sight, as a clear high lip appears at the end of the outer semiconducting layer on the surface of the housing, as shown in the drawing.
Eighth: Replacing the copper tape

1. Pull the copper earth mesh, spread it out and connect it to the copper tape on both sides, using only the spring clip, or using copper wire soldered with tin carefully so as not to affect the outer semiconducting layer of the cable beneath the copper tape.
Ninth: Reinstating the armouring for armoured cables
1. Strip the outer sheath from both ends over a length of 40 mm to suit the length of the armouring.
2. Connect the two armouring ends with the clamps.
3. Wrap mastic tape over the clamps at both ends.
4. Wrap adhesive tape over the armouring so that the overall diameter is as small as possible.
Tenth: Reinstating the outer sheath
1. Roughen the outer sheath of both cables over a distance of 50 mm and wrap mastic tape over it.
2. Pull the outer protective tube and adjust its position so that it covers 90 mm of the outer sheath of cable No. (1), then shrink it using a suitable flame.
